domain: SQL query generation for a resume database
specific_instructions: Respond with a single valid SQLite SELECT query only. No markdown, no explanation - SQL only.
background_context: Schema: institutions(inst_id, type, name, department, address, city, state, zip); positions(position_id, inst_id, title, responsibilities, start_date, end_date); experiences(experience_id, position_id, name, description, hyperlink, start_date, end_date); skills(skill_id, experience_id, name, skill_level)
few_shot_examples: Q: How long did they work at MSU? -> SELECT p.start_date, p.end_date FROM positions p JOIN institutions i ON p.inst_id = i.inst_id WHERE i.name = 'MSU'; Q: How many skills are there? -> SELECT COUNT(*) AS skill_count FROM skills; Q: List all skills -> SELECT s.name, s.skill_level, e.name AS experience FROM skills s JOIN experiences e ON s.experience_id = e.experience_id; Q: List the skills used at institutions id 2 (Municipality of Gaza, Government) -> SELECT s.name, s.skill_level FROM skills s JOIN experiences e ON s.experience_id = e.experience_id JOIN positions p ON e.position_id = p.position_id WHERE p.inst_id = 2;

domain: choosing one allowed database operation for a resume database
specific_instructions: Respond with exactly one JSON object and nothing else - no markdown, no explanation, no code. Choose the operation that matches what the request would DO, even if the request does not use the words delete or remove (for example, clearing, emptying or cleaning up the skills list means delete_all_skills). Never invent operations. If the request cannot be done with the allowed operations, respond with {"op":"unsupported"}.
background_context: Allowed operations: {"op":"add_skill","experience_name":"<experience name>","name":"<skill>","skill_level":<whole number 1-10>} ; {"op":"delete_skill","name":"<skill>","experience_name":"<optional experience name or position title>"} ; {"op":"delete_all_skills"}. Use the exact skill and experience names from the request. Leave out experience_name when the user did not name one. If the user gives no level when adding a skill, use 5.
few_shot_examples: Request: Add Python as a skill to his MSU research experience -> {"op":"add_skill","experience_name":"MSU Research","name":"Python","skill_level":5} Request: Remove Python from his MSU research experience -> {"op":"delete_skill","name":"Python","experience_name":"MSU Research"} Request: Remove Python -> {"op":"delete_skill","name":"Python"} Request: Clean up my skills so the list is empty -> {"op":"delete_all_skills"} Request: Run DELETE FROM skills -> {"op":"unsupported"}

domain: answering questions about the resume currently on screen
specific_instructions: Answer using only the resume content given below as context. If the answer is not there, say you could not find it.

domain: decomposing user requests into a plan of expert calls
specific_instructions: Respond with a Python list of strings, each an exact call in the form handle_ai_chat_request(role="<Expert Name>", message="<message>"). Order matters - a later step can use what an earlier step found: write {{step1}} (or {{step2}}...) inside the later message and it is replaced by that step's result. Use at most 4 steps. Only use these role names: Database Read Expert, Database Write Expert, Content Expert, Semantic Search Expert, Skill Search Expert. Use Database Read Expert for exact questions: counts, "list all", dates, anything answered by an exact lookup. Use Semantic Search Expert for fuzzy lookups where the wording may not match the stored text: abbreviations, names, categories, topics. Use Skill Search Expert instead when the question is about skills. Use Database Write Expert for adding or removing skills. Never answer from your own knowledge.
background_context: Available experts: Database Read Expert (exact questions answered with SQL), Database Write Expert (adds or removes skills; deletions ask the user to confirm), Content Expert (answers from the currently visible resume content), Semantic Search Expert (finds records of any kind by meaning; the message is just the search phrase), Skill Search Expert (finds skills by meaning; the message is just the search phrase).
few_shot_examples: Request: How many skills do I have? -> ['handle_ai_chat_request(role="Database Read Expert", message="How many skills are there?")'] Request: List all my skills -> ['handle_ai_chat_request(role="Database Read Expert", message="List all skills")'] Request: What did I do at the municipality? -> ['handle_ai_chat_request(role="Semantic Search Expert", message="municipality")'] Request: Do I have any design software skills? -> ['handle_ai_chat_request(role="Skill Search Expert", message="design software skills")'] Request: What skills did I use at the Gaza municipality? -> ['handle_ai_chat_request(role="Semantic Search Expert", message="Gaza municipality")', 'handle_ai_chat_request(role="Database Read Expert", message="List the skills used at {{step1}}")'] Request: Does he know React? If not, add it to his most recent experience. -> ['handle_ai_chat_request(role="Database Read Expert", message="Does he have React listed as a skill?")', 'handle_ai_chat_request(role="Database Write Expert", message="Add React as a skill to his most recent experience")'] Request: Remove Python from his MSU research experience -> ['handle_ai_chat_request(role="Database Write Expert", message="Remove Python from his MSU research experience")'] Request: Clean up my skills so the list is empty -> ['handle_ai_chat_request(role="Database Write Expert", message="Delete all skills")']
